authority_scope: Constraint programming and optimization as distinct modeling concerns with explicit variables, constraints, feasibility, and optimization objectives.
limitations: This is official product documentation, not an independent ontology ratification or evidence that a local vertical label selects a particular solver family.
The documentation does not determine whether a source occurrence means CP, MIP, LP, or another constrained optimization formulation.
supports: Constraint programming models variables and constraints and searches for feasible solutions under those constraints.
Feasibility and optimization are distinct concerns, so a constrained method label must not silently claim an optimum or a solver implementation.
title: Constraint Optimization | OR-Tools

authority_scope: The documented CP-SAT solver model and its integer-domain and termination-status boundaries.
limitations: This is official product documentation for one solver, not evidence that every constrained optimization occurrence is integer-valued or CP-SAT-compatible.
Solver status names do not supply the local objective, model, resource budget, or acceptable decision threshold.
supports: The documented CP-SAT model uses integer variables and constraints.
The documented solver distinguishes statuses including optimal, feasible, infeasible, model invalid, and unknown.
title: CP-SAT Solver | OR-Tools

authority_scope: Temporal-network semantics in which edge activation timing and temporal ordering affect network processes.
limitations: The paper supports the temporal-network method family but does not identify the local graph schema, time granularity, observation process, or analytical estimand.
It does not establish that a vertical occurrence means event-level temporal networks rather than longitudinal snapshots or another graph representation.
supports: Temporal-network analysis treats the timing of edge activations as part of network structure and dynamics.
Aggregating a temporal network into a static graph can lose temporal ordering and time-respecting connectivity information.
title: Temporal Networks

authority_scope: Process mining as a method family and the discovery, conformance-checking, and enhancement distinction.
limitations: The manifesto supports a process-mining family decomposition but does not determine which subtype applies to each local occurrence.
It does not qualify an event-log source, provider product, runtime, process model, or canonical candidate status.
publisher_or_authors: IEEE Task Force on Process Mining
supports: Process mining is positioned to improve, redesign, control, and support operational business processes.
The manifesto distinguishes process discovery, conformance checking, and enhancement as the three main types of process mining.
title: Process Mining Manifesto

authority_scope: Causal semantics that distinguish ordinary probabilistic conditioning from intervention and structural-equation reasoning.
limitations: The paper supports a causal-method boundary but does not validate causal identification for any local occurrence.
A raw root-cause label does not supply a causal graph, intervention, confounding assumptions, estimand, or refutation evidence.
supports: Causal intervention has semantics distinct from ordinary Bayesian conditioning.
Causal analysis requires explicit intervention and structural-equation semantics rather than an observational association alone.
title: A Causal Calculus for Statistical Research
